abstractText: Discrimination has been a recurring issue in educational settings and has been connected to detrimental results for students, such as poor mental health, diminished sense of belonging, and worse academic achievement. According to studies, discriminatory language is common in colleges and universities, and students from underrepresented groups are especially susceptible to it (Benner et al., 2018. Also, according to ricento T. (2005), language discrimination refers to the unfair or unequal treatment of individuals or groups based on their language or linguistics background. Discrimination is often illegal and can be a horrible and traumatic experience. Individuals are often subjected to prejudice due to their age, sexual preferences (particularly if they have a disability), and, lastly, their gender or sex. Bullying and discrimination often go hand in hand. Negative discrimination typically occurs when someone acts in a way that is intended to irritate or offend the other person. Experiences with discriminatory language frequently have a negative impact on pupils' academic performance and social-emotional health. Moreover, the study discovered that discriminatory language experiences between peers and between teachers and students were especially detrimental to students' academic and social-emotional outcomes. The necessity of creating successful treatments to reduce racism in schools has also been emphasized by researchers (Bell et al., 2019). Effect of Al 2 O 3 substitution for SiO 2 on fluorosilicate glass-ceramics fabricated from fluoride-containing sludge
abstractText: Abstract The safe disposal and resource utilization of industrial fluoride-containing sludge represent a critical environmental challenge. In this study, high-performance fluorcanasite glass-ceramics were successfully synthesized from industrial sludge via a melt-quenching followed by heat treatment method. The effects of equimolar substitution of Al2O3 for SiO2 on the phase composition on the glass network structure, crystallization behavior, mechanical properties, and fluoride leaching were systematically investigated. Structural analyses revealed that lower Al2O3 content (1-1.5 mol%) favored the formation of layered Q3 units, promoting the precipitation of an interlocking lath-like fluorcanasite main phase at 800 °C. Conversely, higher Al2O3 substitution (>2 mol%) induced the precipitation of xonotlite. The optimized fluorcanasite glass-ceramic (1 mol% Al2O3) exhibited exceptional mechanical performance, achieving a maximum flexural strength of 296.71 ± 22.18 MPa, an elastic modulus of 75.33 ± 0.03 GPa, and a fracture toughness of 1.00 ± 0.14 MPa·m1/2. Furthermore, the fluorcanasite crystalline phase effectively immobilizes F- ions, and its layered structure enhances chemical durability. This work provides a promising method for the resource utilization of fluoride-containing sludge.

Targeting a miRNA–mRNA regulatory network to overcome radioresistance in head and neck cancer: identification of I-OMe-AG-538 via transcriptome-guided drug repurposing
abstractText: Abstract Radioresistance is a major obstacle to successful radiotherapy in head and neck cancer (HNC), leading to treatment failure, recurrence, and poor patient outcomes. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators implicated in radiosensitivity, but comprehensive miRNA–mRNA networks driving radioresistance in HNC remain poorly defined. Here, we established isogenic radioresistant (RR) sublines from OECM1 and Detroit HNC cells through long-term fractionated irradiation and performed global miRNA profiling to identify a consistent 25-miRNA signature (12 upregulated oncogenic miRNAs [OncomiRs] and 13 downregulated tumor-suppressive miRNAs [TSmiRs]) associated with radioresistance. Integrative target prediction, pathway enrichment, and network construction revealed that these miRNAs converge on oncogenic modules including receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling, cell motility, and stress/cancer stemness pathways, with central hubs such as EGFR, IGF1R, and MYC. The refined miRNA–mRNA network (68 interaction pairs) highlights key regulatory miRNAs (e.g., miR-199b-5p and miR-522-3p), whose ectopic overexpression significantly enhances radiosensitivity in HNC cells. Transcriptome-guided drug repurposing via the Connectivity Map platform prioritized I-OMe-AG-538, an IGF1R inhibitor ( τ = –87), as the top candidate radiosensitizer. Validation revealed that I-OMe-AG-538 dose-dependently suppressed IGF1R and Erk phosphorylation, reprogrammed the RR miRNA profile by downregulating OncomiRs and upregulating TSmiRs, elevated intracellular ROS levels, and synergistically increased radiosensitivity in clonogenic assays. TCGA-HNSC analysis confirmed that high IGF1R expression is correlated with a poor prognosis and the upregulation of ROS-scavenging genes. These findings elucidate a coordinated miRNA–mRNA regulatory network underlying radioresistance in HNC and identify I-OMe-AG-538 as a promising radiosensitizer that disrupts oncogenic signaling and redox homeostasis by inhibiting IGF1R and miRNAs, suggesting a potential strategy to enhance the efficacy of radiotherapy in refractory HNC.

title: “At Some Point, You Have to Cut the Cord”: Physician Perceptions of NICU-to-PICU Transfers
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Patients undergoing nonemergent neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) to pediatric ICU (PICU) transfer in the United States have complex medical needs and high relative mortality, but there are no best practices guiding these transfers. This qualitative study was designed to address this gap by characterizing facilitators and barriers to effective NICU-to-PICU transfer among physicians. PATIENTS AND METHODS Semistructured individual interviews were conducted with pediatric intensivists and neonatologists purposively sampled from previous national surveys on transfer processes. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and qualitatively analyzed using an iterative process to elicit themes until thematic saturation was reached. RESULTS A total of 21 interviews were conducted among pediatric intensivists (n = 12) and neonatologists (n = 9). Three major themes emerged integral to effective transfer: ICU mutual trust, multidisciplinary presence, and clinician-family partnership. Subthemes of ICU mutual trust were (1) setting patient goals and caregiver expectations and (2) bridging inter-ICU clinical differences, both of which were tied to regular NICU-PICU touchpoints and early communication with families. Tied to the theme of multidisciplinary presence were (3) identifying continuity, in which care overlap was a facilitator and (4) leveraging collective expertise, in which nursing and allied health professionals’ knowledge of long-stay patients are a major asset. Clinician-family partnership was linked to subthemes of (5) prioritizing patient needs and (6) addressing culture shock while not overstating the NICU-PICU differences. CONCLUSIONS In this qualitative study, pediatric intensivists and neonatologists have collectively identified actionable aspects of nonemergent NICU-to-PICU transfer that, if addressed, may benefit patients, families, and providers.

title: Survivalist circularity: theorising fragility and displacement within necessity-driven circular economies
abstractText: The scholarship on circular economy (CE) is increasingly recognising that in low income contexts, repair, reuse, repurposing, second-hand exchange and material recovery may be driven by economic necessity rather than environmental intention. This paper builds on the established necessity-driven circular economy and develops a narrower, mechanism-level construct of survivalist circularity. Survivalist circularity is defined as circular material practices that can only be sustained under a binding material or livelihood constraint. The construct and its boundaries are defined by a purposive conceptual synthesis of CE, informal recovery, sustainable-livelihoods, frugal-innovation, value-retention, measurement and just-transition literatures. Five testable propositions and a two-axis model relate material constraint to institutional support for value retention. The main prediction is conditional displacement, whereby relaxing a binding constraint decreases the necessity-attributable component of circular practice, while total circularity decreases only where designed, institutional, market or value-based drivers do not substitute. Our paper makes four contributions. It theoretically detects a constraint-contingent mechanism and a temporal displacement risk in necessity-driven CE. It distinguishes survivalist circularity from informality, frugal innovation and geographic or poverty labels in terms of construction. Methodologically, it prioritises the distinction between formal CE institutionalisation and directly observed material practice. In policy, it defines institutional substitution as the sequencing of repair access, secondary markets, safe recovery systems and worker protections before or as necessity weakens. Thus the construct is not a label for Global South or low-income circularity generally, but a testable causal regime, whose value for empirical work depends on demonstrating counterfactual dependence on constraint.

Fatal Cannabis-Associated Cardiovascular Toxicity Following High-Potency Cannabis Use
abstractText: Cannabis has been associated with acute cardiovascular complications, including ventricular arrhythmias and myocardial infarction, particularly in otherwise healthy young adults. We report the death of a 28-year-old man who suffered from witnessed ventricular fibrillation while smoking a legally purchased cannabis product labeled as containing 29.9% Δ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ 9 -THC). Sustained return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after ∼50 minutes of resuscitation. Despite intensive care, severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy developed, and life support was withdrawn 6 days later. Serial ECGs demonstrated evolving ischemic abnormalities accompanied by a dynamic rise in cardiac biomarkers. Autopsy revealed a structurally normal heart with widely patent coronary arteries and patchy acute subendocardial myocardial injury/infarction. Antemortem toxicology demonstrated Δ 9 -THC and 11-nor-9-carboxy-Δ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol, confirming cannabis exposure, while comprehensive cardiac genetic testing identified no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants. The integrated clinical, electrocardiographic, toxicological, pathologic, and genetic findings support acute cannabis-associated cardiovascular toxicity occurring in close temporal association with high-potency cannabis use. Transient myocardial ischemia secondary to coronary vasospasm is favored, although primary ventricular arrhythmia with secondary global ischemia-reperfusion injury cannot be excluded retrospectively. This case highlights the importance of comprehensive clinicopathologic investigation when evaluating sudden cardiovascular collapse following cannabis exposure.

Effectiveness of the Eye Care Kit Promotion Program on Screen Time, Digital Eye Strain and Physical Activity in Preschool Children: A Quasi-Experimental Study
abstractText: Eye strain, medically known as asthenopia, and excessive screen time in young children are associated with digital eye strain and insufficient physical activity. However, evidence on family-based, technology-assisted interventions for preschool children in Thailand remains limited. This study investigated the effectiveness of the Eye Care Kit Promotion Program on screen time, digital eye strain, and physical activity among preschool children. Using a quasi-experimental design, 64 parent-child dyads of children aged 4-5 years with excessive screen time were recruited from two kindergartens in Chiang Mai, Thailand. The experimental group (n = 32) participated in the eight-week Eye Care Kit Promotion Program, whereas the control group (n = 32) received usual care. Outcome assessments were conducted at baseline and at Weeks 4 and 8 using the Parent-Reported Screen Time and Physical Activity Questionnaire and the Digital Eye Strain Syndrome Assessment Form for Children. Intervention effects over time between groups were analyzed using generalized estimating equations. The findings showed that the experimental group demonstrated significantly greater reductions in total and smartphone screen time at both post-intervention (Week 4) and follow-up (Week 8), with consistent reductions in weekend screen time compared with the control group. Digital eye strain decreased at follow-up (Week 8), and total physical activity increased at post-intervention (Week 4), particularly light-intensity activity. However, no significant changes in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity were observed. These findings suggest that a family-based, technology-assisted program can help families manage preschoolers’ screen time, prevent visual risks, and encourage age-appropriate physical activity. Family and school nurses are essential in implementing the program to support healthy behaviors and reduce long-term screen-related health risks. However, a multisite study with long-term follow-up is needed.

title: Leptomeningeal metastasis of lung adenocarcinoma presenting as cauda equina syndrome: a case report and literature review
abstractText: Objective This study aims to improve the understanding of the imaging characteristics of leptomeningeal metastasis, particularly in patients presenting with cauda equina syndrome as the initial manifestation, in order to improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce the misdiagnosis rate. Methods A 69-year-old male presented with a 4-month history of lower back pain accompanied by progressive lower limb numbness and gait instability. Non-contrast lumbar MRI performed at another hospital revealed punctate abnormal signal intensity in the cauda equina region, which was overlooked. The patient was treated as having lumbar disc herniation for 3 months without improvement. Chest CT subsequently revealed a left lower lobe pulmonary mass, which was surgically resected. Postoperative pathology confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation. Following surgery, the patient’s lower limb symptoms worsened, with an inability to walk and onset of urinary and fecal incontinence, prompting referral to our hospital. Physical examination revealed bilateral lower limb muscle strength of grade 2. Laboratory tests showed markedly elevated ferritin and mildly elevated NSE. Whole-spine and brain contrast-enhanced MRI were subsequently performed. Results Spinal contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated linear and nodular thickening and enhancement of the leptomeninges from the cervical to lumbar segments, dural thickening and enhancement, and soft tissue within the cauda equina region exhibiting cast-like filling with marked post-contrast enhancement. Brain contrast-enhanced MRI revealed multiple small nodular enhancing lesions. Based on the pathological confirmation of lung adenocarcinoma and the characteristic imaging findings, a probable (type II) diagnosis of extensive intracranial and leptomeningeal metastases was made on imaging grounds alone. The patient received systemic chemotherapy in combination with bevacizumab but had a poor response with rapid disease progression, and died one month after discharge. Conclusion Cauda equina syndrome can be caused by leptomeningeal metastasis from malignant tumors, and the latter should be considered an important differential diagnosis for cauda equina syndrome in elderly patients. Contrast-enhanced MRI is essential for diagnosis, commonly revealing linear or nodular leptomeningeal enhancement, with cast-like thickening and enhancement representing a characteristic manifestation of advanced disease.

title: Clinical outcomes and prognostic factors of Ommaya reservoir-based intrathecal chemotherapy in lung cancer leptomeningeal metastasis: a retrospective cohort study
abstractText: Objectives To evaluate clinical outcomes and identify prognostic determinants in patients with lung cancer leptomeningeal metastasis (LCLM) treated with Ommaya reservoir-based intrathecal (IT) chemotherapy. Method We retrospectively reviewed 154 LCLM patients treated at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (2022-2025). All patients underwent Ommaya reservoir implantation, or combined with VP shunt. IT pemetrexed (30 mg/week) was delivered for 4–6 consecutive weeks. Clinical characteristics, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features were collected. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan–Meier and Cox regression analyses. Results The cohort had a median age of 59 years (IQR, 53-65) with predominance of female sex (59.1%), lung adenocarcinoma (98.1%), and EGFR mutations (76.7%). Median overall survival (OS) for the entire cohort was 331 days (IQR, 266–446). To provide guidance on clinical decision making, we established an exploratory four-tier prognostic system integrating KPS and intracranial pressure (ICP), categorizing patients into distinct prognostic quartiles. Our analysis revealed that among patients with Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) ≥70, a normal ICP was associated with superior survival. Conversely, in patients with KPS ≤ 50, a decrease in intracranial pressure indicates a poorer prognosis for the patients. Multivariate Cox regression identified KPS, extracranial metastasis, MRI morphology, and CSF glucose/protein as independent prognostic factors. A nomogram developed from these variables showed excellent discrimination (AUC = 0.894) and robust calibration. Conclusions This study establishes a practical risk stratification system and a prognostic nomogram to assist individualized clinical decision-making for LCLM patients.

title: Nutritional and hematological determinants of immune reconstitution and development of a predictive model among virologically suppressed people living with HIV
abstractText: Background Despite effective viral suppression achieved through antiretroviral therapy (ART), a substantial proportion of people living with HIV (PLWH) fail to achieve adequate immune reconstitution and remain at increased risk of adverse clinical outcomes. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted among PLWH in Hebei Province, China, who received long-term ART and achieved sustained virological suppression. Immune reconstitution was defined as achieving a CD4 + T cell count ≥350 cells/μL during follow-up. Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed to evaluate the dynamics of immune recovery and identify independent predictors associated with time to immune reconstitution. A prognostic model was developed and evaluated using Harrell’s concordance index (C-index), time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration analysis, and 1,000-times bootstrap internal validation. Results During a median follow-up of 4.02 years (95% CI: 4.00–4.04 years), 1,651 (76.9%) participants achieved immune reconstitution, whereas 495 (23.1%) did not achieve immune reconstitution. The probability of immune recovery increased rapidly during the first year after ART initiation and subsequently plateaued. Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that older age, advanced WHO clinical stage, and lower baseline CD4 + T cell count were independently associated with a reduced probability of immune reconstitution. In addition, overweight status (BMI ≥ 24 kg/m2; HR = 1.12, 95% CI: 1.02–1.23, p = 0.021) and higher baseline hemoglobin levels (HR = 1.004, 95% CI: 1.001–1.007, p = 0.016) were independently associated with improved immune recovery after adjustment for established clinical and immunological factors. The prediction model demonstrated good discrimination (C-index = 0.713), with time-dependent AUCs of 0.849, 0.874, and 0.850 at 1, 2, and 4 years, respectively. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed immune recovery probabilities. Conclusion Approximately one-quarter of virologically suppressed PLWH did not achieve immune reconstitution after long-term ART. Immune recovery occurred predominantly during the first year after ART initiation. In addition to established predictors such as age, baseline CD4 + T cell count, and WHO clinical stage, BMI and hemoglobin levels may serve as readily obtainable clinical indicators reflecting nutritional reserve and overall health status. The developed prediction model may provide a practical approach for identifying individuals with delayed immune recovery and supporting individualized clinical monitoring.

Evaluating zinc bioavailability in dredged sediments of Guanabara bay (BRAZIL): implications for coastal management standards
abstractText: Abstract Guanabara Bay (GB) is an environment contaminated by metals, and it is the bay that receives the most dredging in Brazil and South America. Previous studies have shown the impact of dredging on planktonic and benthic species, which were not correctly measured by the Brazilian dredging standard CONAMA Resolution 454/12 (2012). Given this, the present study compared two acid extractions targeting metal bioavailability (1 M HCl and acetic acid) in sediments from four areas of GB sampled in summer and winter, before and after resuspension. The results showed that Zn concentrations exceeded the standard in all samples in extractions methods and in two seasons after resuspension. In winter, three of the four areas showed concentrations exceeding levels 1 and 2 of CONAMA Resolution 454/12 (2012), both before and after resuspension. The bioavailability change index (BC) was applied to show the remobilization of metals in the sediment after dredging. Results evidenced that Zn remobilization occurred after resuspension for all samples and in most resuspension intervals, indicating an environmental risk related to the resuspension activity. This demonstrates the efficiency of using bioavailable extractions for the monitoring of dredging activities. In addition to being cheaper and easier to perform than the pseudo-total extractions recommended in most global standards, it provides valuable information for improving dredging management policies. According to the results, a revision of the dredging standard is recommended, considering the inclusion of bioavailable extractions.

title: Development and internal temporal validation of an explainable XGBoost model for predicting clinical pregnancy after frozen embryo transfer
abstractText: Key message An explainable machine learning model was developed using comprehensive clinical variables to predict clinical pregnancy outcomes following frozen embryo transfer. Compared with conventional statistical models, the extreme gradient boosting–based model showed numerically higher discrimination and provided interpretable insights through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, supporting individualized decision-making in reproductive medicine. Research question Can an interpretable XGBoost-based model leveraging multi-feature clinical data better predict pregnancy outcomes after frozen embryo transfer (FET) compared to conventional logistic regression? Design This retrospective single-center study included 1,319 patients who underwent FET. Participants were temporally split into a training cohort (n=1,013) and a temporal validation cohort (n=306) according to the date of embryo transfer. Pre-transfer demographic, hormonal, treatment, and ultrasonographic variables were collected. An XGBoost model was developed and compared with logistic regression by assessing discrimination (area under the ROC curve [AUC] and area under the precision–recall curve [AUPRC]), calibration (calibration curves, Brier score, intercept, and slope), and clinical utility using decision curve analysis (DCA). Model interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results The XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.854 (95% CI 0.832–0.877) in training and 0.722 (95% CI 0.666–0.779) in temporal validation, with corresponding AUPRC values of 0.840 and 0.707. Calibration in the temporal validation cohort was acceptable (Brier score 0.212; calibration intercept 0.056; slope 0.965). DCA indicated a positive net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds, with high sensitivity at a representative probability threshold of 0.30. SHAP visualizations provided feature-level and individual-level explanations. Conclusion Using single-center data, we developed and internally, temporally validated an explainable XGBoost model for predicting clinical pregnancy after FET. The model delivers accurate, interpretable predictions that may support personalized decision-making and facilitate the clinical integration of artificial intelligence into assisted reproductive medicine.

Comparing simulation and physical kilobots performance in two ant-inspired foraging behaviours
abstractText: Robotics looks to nature for inspiration to perform effectively in unstructured environments and can be used to test biological hypotheses. Social animals often share information about food source locations like tandem running in ants, where a leader guides a naive recruit to a known profitable food site. This is extremely advantageous as it allows the sharing of important information among colony members, but it also has costs, such as waiting time inside the nest when no leaders are around, and a reduced walking speed for the tandem couple compared to individuals. Whether and when these costs outweigh the benefits is not well understood as it is challenging to study complex social behaviours in nature. We developed two kilobot-based approaches to compare tandem running and lone scout foraging (using an isotropic random walk) where an ant searches for food without any previous knowledge of its location: one approach based on real-life experiments and the other one on computer simulations. We tested whether the simulation-based comparison of the two bio-inspired strategies reliably predict the performance in the real-life scenario and we investigated the role that the size of the search arena played in the effectiveness of foraging. Tandem pairs discovered the food source faster in real-life experiments; however, this result was reversed in the simulations. These results highlight the inconsistencies between simulation and real-life experiments, previously reported for other systems and known as reality gap, and show how the use of simulations can lead to qualitatively different conclusions about the relative effectiveness of bio-inspired foraging strategies.

A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW ON APICULTURE AND HONEY RESEARCH, HONEY FRAUD, HONEY PHARMACOPEIA AND FDA-APPROVED HONEY PRODUCTS, CLINICAL EFFICACY OF HONEY PHARMACEUTICAL PRODUCTS, HONEY CONTAMINATION WITH CONSUMER HEALTH RISKS WITH ONE HEALTH PERSPECTIVE
abstractText: Background: Honey is a divine gift from Allah, described in the Quran as a source of healing for mankind, and Allah urges people to think (do research) about honey. Scientists have found that honey is an insect-derived natural sweetener rich in antioxidants, antimicrobials, and essential nutrients that support immune function, offer therapeutic benefits and promote healing, and have cosmetic and industrial value. But adulteration and fake honey production by dishonest people (a clear sin/haram) have severely damaged the global honey industry by undercutting honest beekeepers, misleading consumers, threatening pollinator populations, and depriving people of Allah's divine gift. Objectives: This review describes apiculture and honey research from ancient to modern times; honey fraud, pharmacopeia and FDA-approved honey products, clinical efficacy of honey pharmaceuticals, and honey contamination with consumer health risks with a ‘One Health’ perspective Materials and Methods: A narrative review of Google Scholar, PubMed, and other databases identified 580 relevant research reports on different aspects of honey to meet the objectives of this review. In addition, seven sources of honey, four from different Facebook vendors and three from supermarkets, were examined to detect adulteration and contamination in Bangladesh. Results: Honey is Allah’s gift to mankind, but this review shows that finding authentic honey in supermarkets globally is increasingly difficult because of complex global supply-chain blending and widespread economic adulteration with cheap sugar syrups. Reports show that 46% of imported honey and 96% of supermarket honeys in the UK, up to 70% in the US, 75 to 86.5% in the Philippines, up to 75% of Chinese honey, 93% in Turkey, and 77% of Indian honeys are adulterated. Global honey exports have increased by 67%, while honey production has increased by only 15%, indicating that the world is selling more honey than bees can produce. Reviews also show that all nine popular imported honey brands and seven locally produced honeys available in the Bangladeshi market are adulterated. Fake and adulterated honey poses significant metabolic syndrome, organ damage, systemic health risks, potential carcinogenic effects, and allergic reactions, often worsening conditions like Type II diabetes and obesity. Medical-grade honey (MGH) has shown strong antibacterial activity against both MDR (multidrug-resistant) and non-MDR bacteria, is effective against biofilm formation, and is also effective in diabetic patients with infected foot ulcers. This review compares the clinical efficacy of pharmaceutical honey products, including their indications, uses, and efficacy. This review examines research on apiculture and honey research, including honeybee diseases and human health risks. Reported risks include infant botulism (Cl. botulinum spores), gastroenteritis (Bacillus cereus, Cl. perfringens, Salmonella spp., Shigella spp., Staphylococcus aureus), yeast and mold infections, and antibiotic-resistant bacterial problems. The interaction between honey contaminants, wound healing, and the ‘One Health’ framework centers on managing chronic or infected wounds by recognizing the deep links between human medicine, veterinary care, and environmental factors. This collaborative approach is vital to stop the spread of dangerous pathogens and combat drug resistance. Conclusion: This review suggests that there is no guarantee of getting authentic honey from local or imported sources on the global market, including Bangladesh. The only way to guarantee authentic honey from a local producer is to see it coming out of the hive (but not bee sugar syrup feeding honey), or to produce our own honey ourselves. These indicate that Allah’s gift of pure honey has healing properties, and original Islam is viewed as the complete and final guidance sent by Allah for humanity, but both have lost their originality or been modified to an unacceptable status. However, MGH's especially authentic manuka honey-based formulations are FDA-approved, and their clinical efficacy supports the Quranic verses in which Allah says honey has healing properties. Modern laboratory tests needed to detect sophisticated honey adulterants are not currently available for routine testing. A ‘One Health’ approach to honey fraud control integrates human health, animal (bee) health, and environmental stewardship with systemic governance to protect product integrity.

Empowering Oyster Mushroom Farmers through IoT-Based Smart Mushroom House for Climate Adaptation
abstractText: Climate variability challenges oyster mushroom cultivation by disrupting optimal temperature and humidity conditions, particularly during the dry season. This community engagement program aimed to implement an Internet of Things (IoT)-based Smart Mushroom House system to support adaptive and sustainable mushroom cultivation. The program was conducted with the Alugoro Youth Farmer Group in Sragen Regency, Indonesia, using a Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) approach involving socialization, training, IoT installation, assistance, and evaluation. The GrowMatic system integrated temperature and humidity sensors with automated irrigation control for real-time environmental management. Results showed improved farmer knowledge, with average scores increasing from 5.3 to 10.4 out of 11 questions (96.2% improvement). The system maintained cultivation conditions at 25–26°C temperature and 82–90% humidity while enabling farmers to operate the technology independently. This program demonstrates the potential of IoT-based solutions combined with participatory capacity building to strengthen climate-resilient oyster mushroom agribusiness.

title: Ultrasound-guided hydrodissection combined with radiofrequency for refractory occipital neuralgia: clinical outcomes, durability, and factors associated with repeat intervention
abstractText: Objective To evaluate clinical outcomes after ultrasound-guided hydrodissection combined with radiofrequency treatment for occipital neuralgia secondary to greater occipital nerve (GON) entrapment and to explore factors independently associated with repeat intervention. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 81 patients with GON entrapment who underwent ultrasound-guided hydrodissection combined with radiofrequency treatment at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital between February 2024 and June 2025. The mean follow-up was 12.39 months. Pain intensity, headache-related disability, and depressive symptoms were assessed preoperatively and 3 months after treatment using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS), and 10-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CESD-10), respectively. Kaplan–Meier analysis was used to estimate the median duration of symptom relief. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with repeat intervention. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine an optimal cutoff, and subgroup analyses were conducted to assess the consistency of the association. Results At 3 months, the mean VAS score decreased from 6.56 ± 1.63 preoperatively to 1.88 ± 1.05, MIDAS grades improved significantly, and the mean CESD-10 score decreased from 12.41 ± 7.26 to 7.63 ± 5.14 (all p < 0.05). The proportion of patients satisfied with treatment was 87.7%. One patient experienced local anesthetic systemic toxicity, corresponding to a complication rate of 1.23%. The median duration of symptom relief was 6 months. Multivariable logistic regression identified age as independently associated with repeat intervention (OR, 0.947; p = 0.022), with an optimal cutoff of 56.5 years. The inverse association between age and repeat intervention was generally consistent across prespecified subgroups, with no statistically significant interactions (all P for interaction > 0.05). Conclusion In this retrospective single-arm cohort, ultrasound-guided hydrodissection combined with radiofrequency treatment was associated with improvements in pain, headache-related disability, and depressive symptoms, together with high patient satisfaction. Older age was independently associated with a lower likelihood of repeat intervention.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis small RNAs MTS0997 and MTS1338 regulate both pathogen virulence and host immune responses
abstractText: Previously, others and we demonstrated that small RNAs MTS1338 and MTS0997 of Mycobacterium tuberculosis , the causative agent of tuberculosis (TB), are essential for persistence inside host macrophages. However, their role in mycobacterial transcriptional profile regulation was characterized incompletely, and potential influence on host immune responses and the outcome of infection remained obscure. To obtain new insights in M. tuberculosis biology and TB pathogenesis we established unmarked single-knockout (KO) M. tuberculosis strains with deleted genes for MTS0997, or MTS1338, as well as the double KO strain. These strains, their parental wild type progenitor and complemented double KO variant were explored in three experimental settings: (i) whole genome expression profiling during cultural growth, (ii) whole genome transcriptional analysis of murine bone marrow-derived macrophages activated or not with IFN-γ, and (iii) TB infection in genetically highly TB-susceptible mice. The results of our experiments indicate that deletion of MTS0997 sRNA results in a more pronounced impact on M. tuberculosis biology compared to MTS1338. The most prominent phenotypic shifts in MTS0997 -deleted strain were modulation of bacterial succinate/fumarate respiration, up-regulation of genes belonging to the ESX-1 secretion system, increase in pathogen virulence for the murine host and decreased production of a few pro-inflammatory cytokines in the lung tissue. In addition, differences in the sizes of B-cell and other MHC-II-expressing cell populations in lungs of mice infected with single- compared to double-KO strains provided evidence for transcriptional epistasis, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood in mycobacteria.

Machine learning-based prediction of lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma: an interpretable multidimensional model
abstractText: Background Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is a prevalent feature in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) that significantly influences surgical management and prognosis. Accurate identification of LNM risk is essential for optimizing adjuvant therapy and long-term surveillance strategies in clinical practice. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 232 patients who underwent thyroidectomy. We employed LASSO regression to select six predictive features from a comprehensive covariate panel. Subsequently, seven machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated via grid search and 5-fold cross-validation. The optimal model was interpreted using SHAP analysis to elucidate feature contributions. Results LASSO-based feature selection retained six predictive features: BRAF mutation status, tumor size, capsular invasion, extrathyroidal extension, multifocality, and TSH. Among the seven algorithms, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) model showed the most favorable validation performance, achieving an AUC of 0.849 (95% CI, 0.756–0.934) and an accuracy of 0.768 in the validation cohort. SHAP analysis identified TSH and tumor size as the most influential contributors to model predictions, enabling transparent and individualized LNM risk stratification. Conclusion The SVM-based model demonstrated favorable internal validation performance and provided an interpretable framework for individualized LNM risk stratification in patients with PTC. Further prospective multicenter validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Frontal Gamma Asymmetry as a Forensic Tool for Emotional Valence in a Murder Case Study
abstractText: In criminal cases, forensic evaluations often hinge on determining a defendant’s competence and intent. Assessing underlying emotional states presents unique challenges, as self‑reports may be unreliable or incomplete. In this exploratory single‑case study, we illustrate how psychological assessments can be combined with quantitative EEG (qEEG) and source localization techniques to examine neural markers of emotional processing in the context of a murder trial. Emotional valence toward key individuals and events was derived from a proprietary frontal gamma asymmetry protocol. Although this innovative metric offers unique insights, it has received limited independent replication and should therefore be interpreted cautiously and in conjunction with established measures such as frontal alpha asymmetry. Key procedural covariates, including the defendant’s medication (sertraline), were documented because serotonergic agents can modulate baseline asymmetry patterns. Findings indicated general alignment between neural patterns and reported affect, but we emphasize that these observations reflect preliminary insights from a single individual and require validation in larger samples before supporting broader forensic applications.

Pengaruh Literasi Digital, Literasi AI, dan Berpikir Kritis terhadap Kemampuan Masyarakat Menyaring Informasi di Era Kecerdasan Buatan
abstractText: Pesatnya perkembangan kecerdasan buatan (AI) telah mengubah cara informasi diproduksi, didistribusikan, dan dikonsumsi, sekaligus meningkatkan risiko misinformasi, konten yang dimanipulasi, dan informasi hasil AI yang tidak dapat diandalkan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji pengaruh literasi digital, literasi kecerdasan buatan, dan berpikir kritis terhadap kemampuan masyarakat dalam menyaring informasi di era kecerdasan buatan di Indonesia. Pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatori digunakan dengan melibatkan 150 responden yang dipilih melalui teknik *purposive sampling*. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner terstruktur dengan skala Likert lima poin dan dianalisis menggunakan IBM SPSS Statistics versi 25. Analisis yang dilakukan meliputi uji validitas dan reliabilitas, uji asumsi klasik, regresi linear berganda, uji-t, uji-F, dan koefisien determinasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa literasi digital memiliki pengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kemampuan menyaring informasi, sementara literasi kecerdasan buatan juga menunjukkan pengaruh positif dan signifikan. Berpikir kritis menunjukkan pengaruh signifikan yang paling kuat terhadap kemampuan menyaring informasi. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel tersebut berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kemampuan masyarakat dalam menyaring informasi, dengan menjelaskan 58,1% varians data. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa penguatan ketahanan informasi masyarakat di era AI memerlukan kombinasi terpadu antara kompetensi digital, pemahaman khusus mengenai AI, dan penalaran kritis. Berpikir kritis muncul sebagai faktor yang paling berpengaruh, yang menegaskan pentingnya evaluasi berbasis bukti saat menghadapi informasi digital maupun informasi yang dihasilkan oleh AI.

Electrophysiological signature of stroke recovery: investigating EEG biomarkers for prognostic insights
abstractText: Introduction Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, often resulting in persistent motor impairments that reflect disruptions in large-scale brain networks. An integrated framework capturing spatiotemporal EEG dynamics would help clarify how these networks change during recovery. Methods We analysed resting-state EEG from stroke patients at 1 week (Session 1) and three months (Session 2) post-stroke to investigate electrophysiological biomarkers of motor recovery, indexed by change in the Fugl-Meyer scale (Δ FM ). We quantified relative alpha-band power, microstate metrics (mean duration, complexity, and transition probabilities), and measures of metastability and synchrony derived from the Kuramoto Order Parameter. Results:s Change in relative alpha power emerged as the strongest single correlate of motor improvement, accounting for the largest proportion of variance among the EEG measures examined. Metastability and synchrony did not individually reach statistical significance but showed moderate positive correlations with Δ FM , particularly in the alpha and theta bands, and added 26% explained variance in Δ FM when combined with alpha power. Microstate parameters did not explain additional variance once alpha power and network-level dynamics were accounted for. A hierarchical model combining alpha power, metastability/synchrony, and microstates explained over 78% of the variance in Δ FM . Discussion These findings indicate that stroke recovery involves restoring balanced alpha oscillations and flexible large-scale brain coordination. Larger samples and more frequent longitudinal assessments are required to confirm the prognostic utility of integrated EEG biomarkers for guiding personalised stroke rehabilitation strategies.

title: Laboratory-based case finding using phosphate and alkaline phosphatase to identify genetic and nutritional rickets in children
abstractText: Introduction Hypophosphatemic rickets is a rare disease characterized by renal phosphate loss, leading to chronic hypophosphatemia, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and skeletal symptoms that may remain unnoticed until advanced stages. Early diagnosis is essential because effective treatment is available to reduce complications. Objectives To evaluate a laboratory-based case-finding strategy for identifying oligosymptomatic patients with hypophosphatemic rickets using phosphorus and alkaline phosphatase results in a pediatric population. Methods A descriptive observational study was conducted in patients under 18 years of age at a tertiary care hospital between June 2021 and July 2025. Of 47,127 phosphorus or alkaline phosphatase measurements requested, 45,923 measurements corresponding to 28,045 tests from 12,513 patients were analyzed after exclusions. Test showing hypophosphatemia and/or elevated alkaline phosphatase were identified, and X-rays and clinical data were reviewed for classification. Results A total of 22,860 phosphorus measurements and 23,063 alkaline phosphatase measurements were analyzed, with both parameters available in 17,878 laboratory tests. Hypophosphatemia was observed in 2,281 phosphorus measurements (9.98%), and elevated alkaline phosphatase in 3,301 measurements (14.3%). Fifty-five laboratory tests (0.31%) from 37 patients simultaneously met the criteria for hypophosphatemia (<−2 SD) and elevated alkaline phosphatase (>+2 SD); 56.8% were male, with a mean age of 6.5 ± 6.0 years. Following clinical review, 15 patients (40.5%) were classified as having a bone mineral metabolism disorder, including 10 with osteopenia of prematurity, three with nutritional rickets, one with a pathogenic variant in PHEX , and one with osteoporosis in the context of ReNU syndrome; 10 patients (27.0%) were classified in the acute/critical illness group and 12 (32.4%) in the other category. Radiographs were available in 30 patients, with findings consistent with rickets in three (10%). One previously unrecognized case of mild nutritional rickets was identified. Conclusions Laboratory-based case finding using phosphorus and alkaline phosphatase may help identify pediatric bone metabolism disorders, including forms of rickets. Combined hypophosphatemia and elevated alkaline phosphatase may be useful for guiding etiological investigation. This approach may complement clinical evaluation and facilitate earlier diagnosis. Early identification is clinically relevant because treatments can modify disease course and reduce long-term complications in children with confirmed forms of rickets, when appropriate.

title: Designing a framework for Sustainable Smart Agriculture with Mobile Robots and CNN
abstractText: Advances in artificial intelligence, robotics, and computer vision enable intelligent gardening systems that reduce manual monitoring. This study presents a smart gardening framework integrating a mobile robot with convolutional neural network (CNN) flower recognition. The robot captures garden images, while the CNN classifies flower species and provides plant-specific information for future care decisions. Using 50 training images and 50 independent testing images, the model achieved 92.0% training accuracy and 95.0% testing accuracy. The framework connects robotic image acquisition with automated visual recognition and provides a foundation for future irrigation, fertilization, and autonomous garden-management functions.

Three-dimensional anatomical reconstruction as a guideline-anchored framework for choosing between lung-sparing resection and image-guided ablation in deep subsolid pulmonary nodules: a thoracic surgeon’s perspective
abstractText: Low-dose computed tomography screening has markedly increased the detection of small, deeply located subsolid pulmonary nodules, and local therapy for these lesions now encompasses anatomical segmentectomy, tailored sublobar resection, lobectomy, and image-guided thermal ablation. Although multidisciplinary pathways already inform modality selection, three-dimensional (3D) anatomical reconstruction - despite its established role in segmentectomy planning - is rarely used as a shared patient-specific dataset to guide both resection and ablation decisions. In this perspective, a thoracic surgeon argues that, for a deep or cross-segment subsolid nodule with an established indication for local therapy, a single patient-specific 3D dataset can inform both branches of the decision. The same volumetric anatomy - including nodule size and consolidation-to-tumor ratio, segmental boundaries, bronchovascular relationships, pleura, and the chest wall - is first used to determine whether adequate-margin lung-sparing resection is achievable and, if it is not, to assess whether ablation is anatomically feasible through three sequential filters: trajectory safety, perilesional structural risk, and predicted ablative coverage. The approach is illustrated with a representative case and discussed in the contexts of multifocal disease, the post-resection lung, and perivascular lesions, together with the trade-offs associated with forgoing nodal staging and tissue diagnosis. The framework does not expand indications beyond those already supported by guidelines. Rather, it operationalizes these recommendations through patient-specific anatomy, with the aim of making modality selection more transparent, reproducible, and auditable. It remains an unvalidated, single-center proposal that requires prospective evaluation.

Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive multilayer economic networks: a stability-guarded potential game framework
abstractText: Complex economic and social systems emerge from repeated strategic interactions on networks whose links also change with behavior. Existing evolutionary-game models commonly assume fixed-interaction structures, whereas adaptive-network approaches often lack a global incentive certificate and an explicit stability condition. This paper develops a co-evolutionary multilayer potential game, in which boundedly rational agents update mixed strategies, while market, information, and institutional links adapt to observed compatibility and diffusion signals. We propose a stability-guarded mirror-replicator (SGMR) dynamic that combines entropy-regularized strategy revision, projected link rewiring, and a spectral safeguard. The mirror step is shown to recover replicator dynamics in the small-step limit. We prove the exact-potential property, monotone potential improvement, sublinear stationarity, and local input-to-state stability under observation disturbances. Computational experiments on synthetic economic networks show faster convergence, higher collective welfare, stronger resilience to noise, and more stable network adaptation than static mirror ascent, standard replicator dynamics, and fictitious play. Additional diagnostics directly evaluate the input-to-state stability bound, quantify the empirical residual decay, and confirm statistically significant welfare gains across network topologies. This framework links evolutionary dynamics, adaptive multilayer networks, and decentralized collective decision-making in complex social systems.

title: Physiological load and circadian organization of cardiovascular, autonomic and thermal functions in dry and lactating ewes assessed using biologgers
abstractText: Context Lactation is a physiologically demanding period in sheep that is characterized by an increase in metabolic and cardiovascular requirements. Although physiological changes during lactation have been well documented, less is known about how lactation affects the circadian organization of cardiovascular and autonomic functions. Aim The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of lactation on physiological load and circadian organization in adult ewes. Methods Five lactating ewes that were in the second to third week of lactation with lambs present, were compared to seven dry ewes. Subcutaneous biologgers recorded body temperature (T), heart rate (HR), and heart rate variability (HRV; standard deviation of normal-to-normal R–R intervals [SDNN] and root mean square of consecutive deviations between normal heartbeats [RMSSD]) every 30 min for 20 days. Raw physiological data and circadian parameters derived from 24-h cosinor models, including midline-estimating statistic of rhythm (MESOR), amplitude, acrophase, robustness, and circadianity, were evaluated. Key results Lactating ewes exhibited higher T and HR than dry ewes. SDNN was lower in lactating ewes, whereas RMSSD showed a non-significant tendency to be lower. Both groups exhibited robust 24-h rhythms in HR, although rhythms in lactating ewes had higher MESOR, amplitude, and robustness. Circadian organization of HRV was less consistent in lactating ewes, with fewer animals exhibiting significant circadian rhythms and greater inter-individual variability than in dry ewes. Dry ewes exhibited a lower physiological load and a more stable and coherent circadian organization than did lactating ewes. Conclusion Lactation in ewes is associated with an increase in cardiovascular and thermal load, a reduction in autonomic variability, and marked changes in circadian regulation, particularly autonomic rhythmicity. Implications Integrating circadian analysis with conventional physiological measurements provides a more comprehensive assessment of physiological status and might provide sensitive indicators of functional strain during lactation.

The effect of project-based learning on students’ motivation in school-based physical Education and behavioral intention toward sport participation: a theoretical and empirical perspective in educational sport contexts
abstractText: This study examined the association of Project-Based Learning (PBL) with students’ motivation in physical education (PE) and behavioral intention toward sport participation within an integrated theoretical framework combining Self-Determination Theory (SDT), constructivist learning theory, and social cognitive theory. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design involved 120 secondary school students from eight intact classes, with four classes assigned to PBL ( n = 60) and four to traditional instruction ( n = 60). The 12-week intervention comprised structured sport-based PBL activities, whereas the control condition used predominantly teacher-centered instruction. Intervention effects were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models (LMM) accounting for repeated measurements and class-level clustering, followed by a baseline-adjusted two-level parallel mediation analysis accounting for students nested within classes. Significant group × time interactions favored PBL for overall motivation ( p < 0.001, d = 1.60), intrinsic motivation ( d = 1.67), identified regulation ( d = 1.35), and behavioral intention ( d = 1.48; all p < 0.001). Significant group × time interactions were also observed for psychological needs satisfaction, including autonomy ( d = 1.72), competence ( d = 1.80), and relatedness ( d = 1.62), as well as self-efficacy ( d = 1.70; all p < 0.001). Psychological needs satisfaction [ B = 0.21, 95% CI (0.04, 0.38)] and self-efficacy [ B = 0.16, 95% CI (0.02, 0.30)] showed significant indirect effects on post-intervention motivation, while the direct effect remained significant [ B = 0.29, 95% CI (0.04, 0.54)], with a total effect of B = 0.66, 95% CI (0.37, 0.95), a pattern consistent with significant indirect associations. Because the mediators and outcome were assessed concurrently at posttest, these indirect effects should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of causal mediation. These findings indicate that PBL was associated with greater improvements in motivational and psychological outcomes and that psychological needs satisfaction and self-efficacy may represent complementary pathways linking PBL with students’ motivation toward PE and behavioral intentions toward continued sport participation.

title: Student Leaders’ Social Media Engagement Shaping Online-to-Offline Activism in a Teacher’s College
abstractText: Social media is an emerging arena where students are practicing leadership in both virtual and physical realities. While previous studies have established the association between social media engagement and activism, there is a need to document how such online activity is connected to extra-online manifestations, particularly in selected teacher education institutions in the Philippines. Hence, this study explored how social media helped these students perform their empowerment-based activism in the real world. Informed by Kelman’s Social Influence Theory, the descriptions provided by nine (9) organization chairpersons and vice chairpersons selected through purposive sampling became the basis of this study’s findings. After transcribing the responses to the semi-structured interview guide presented through Google Forms, the researchers applied Braun and Clarke’s (2006) thematic analysis. This study found that students’ activism was actualized through the online medium via increased mobilization, leadership skill development, ethically guided conduct, and response to online challenges. Contrary to activism’s performative nature, the respondents prioritized information gathering, decision-making, cooperation, and leadership in promoting civic responsibility. As such, this study’s results added to the existing scholarship on social media’s role in activism while highlighting the importance of empowerment-based leadership in teacher education.

Hepatobiliary phase imaging in HCC: revisiting diagnostic algorithms and clinical utility of gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI across international guidelines
abstractText: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. In at-risk populations, noninvasive imaging diagnosis relies primarily on the vascular hallmarks of arterial phase hyperenhancement and washout appearance. However, these features are often absent in early hepatocarcinogenesis, thereby limiting timely detection. Gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI has expanded the role of imaging in HCC, yet its clinical value is often oversimplified as a comparison of diagnostic performance with CT or extracellular contrast MRI. A critical issue is that the same imaging feature, particularly hepatobiliary phase (HBP) hypointensity, carries different diagnostic consequences across international frameworks. Because HBP signal loss reflects early hepatocellular dysfunction that may precede typical vascular hallmarks, gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI provides a biologically driven sensitivity advantage for detecting small and early-stage HCC. However, its apparent performance varies largely according to diagnostic intent: sensitivity-oriented Asian guidelines incorporate HBP hypointensity as a major feature to enable earlier detection, whereas Western guidelines prioritize specificity in high-stakes decision contexts, such as liver transplantation, and therefore restrict its diagnostic weight. This intent-dependent interpretation explains much of the inconsistency reported in the literature and underscores the limitations of pooled, guideline-agnostic performance estimates. Beyond diagnosis, HBP imaging also offers complementary information for assessing treatment response, although it remains underutilized in current criteria. Overall, the clinical value of gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI lies not in universal superiority but in context-aligned application, shifting the focus from modality comparison to optimization according to downstream clinical consequences. Key Points Question Gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI is interpreted differently across international hepatocellular carcinoma diagnostic guidelines, resulting in uncertainty regarding optimal imaging criteria and clinical decision-making. Findings Hepatobiliary phase hypointensity reflects early hepatocellular dysfunction and improves sensitivity for small and early-stage HCC, but its impact varies according to diagnostic intent. Critical Relevance Statement An intent-aligned interpretation strategy may help reconcile guideline heterogeneity and optimize the use of gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI, particularly in the evaluation of small HCC.

title: A multi-centre study on cervical cancer screening reveals population-related impact on cervical intraepithelial neoplasia rate
abstractText: Objective To conduct a three-year cervical cancer screen in Zhejiang, Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia and analyse clinical and population data to identify possible improvements to the screening protocol. Methods A standard protocol including human papillomavirus (HPV) detection, cytology test, colposcopy, and histopathology inspection was adapted for the screening. Additional HPV genotyping was performed for participants in Sichuan, Beijing, and Inner Mongolia. Results 12,086 women were included in this study, and 178 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) were identified. Detailed analyses on features of age, region, ethnicity, and origin showed a notable correlation between age strata and high-grade CIN rates. Moreover, apart from HPV16/18, other HPV types such as HPV33, HPV52, and HPV58 were found to be enriched in high-grade CIN cases, as was repeat positivity. Conclusions Our results suggest that age, HPV16, and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) are prominent exploratory predictors for CIN2+ detection, and HPV33, 52, and 58 may pose higher risks than other non-HPV16/18 types. Future studies incorporating prospective effectiveness and health-economic evaluation are required to validate the clinical utility of these predictors.

title: Pengaruh Kompetensi SDM, Sistem Informasi Akuntansi, dan Pengendalian Internal terhadap Kualitas Penerapan Akuntansi Murabahah melalui Kepatuhan PSAK 102 sebagai Variabel Mediasi
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh Kompetensi SDM, Sistem Informasi Akuntansi, dan Pengendalian Internal terhadap Kualitas Penerapan Akuntansi Murabahah melalui Kepatuhan PSAK 102 sebagai variabel mediasi pada KSPPS BMT Mandiri Sejahtera Jawa Timur. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatori dengan 135 responden yang dipilih melalui purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner skala Likert dan dianalisis menggunakan Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) dengan SmartPLS 4. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Kompetensi SDM tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Kualitas Penerapan Akuntansi Murabahah (p-value 0,742), sedangkan Sistem Informasi Akuntansi berpengaruh signifikan (p-value 0,007). Pengendalian Internal tidak berpengaruh signifikan (p-value 0,064), sedangkan Kepatuhan PSAK 102 berpengaruh signifikan (p-value 0,001). Kepatuhan PSAK 102 memediasi pengaruh Kompetensi SDM terhadap Kualitas Penerapan Akuntansi Murabahah (p-value 0,037), tetapi tidak memediasi pengaruh Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dan Pengendalian Internal. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kualitas penerapan akuntansi murabahah dipengaruhi secara langsung oleh Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dan Kepatuhan PSAK 102, sedangkan pengaruh Kompetensi SDM menjadi signifikan melalui Kepatuhan PSAK 102.

Empirical Analysis of Goal Hijacking in Large Vision-Language Models via Visual Prompt Injection
abstractText: Abstract In this study, we explore visual prompt injection (VPI), a method that exploits the ability of large vision-language models (LVLMs) to follow instructions embedded within input images. LVLMs, such as GPT-4V, are designed to interpret and respond to visual prompts. Although this capability enables valuable applications, it introduces substantial security risks. To address this issue, we propose a new VPI method called “goal hijacking via visual prompt injection” (GHVPI). This method redirects LVLMs from their original execution task to an alternative task specified by an attacker. Our quantitative analysis reveals that GPT-4V is vulnerable to GHVPI, with an attack success rate of 15.8%, posing a significant security risk. Our results also reveal that GHVPI success relies on the character recognition and instruction-following capabilities of LVLMs. These findings highlight a critical vulnerability, raising concerns regarding the secure deployment of LVLMs in practical applications. Future research should prioritize developing robust mitigation strategies to address these vulnerabilities and facilitate the secure integration of LVLMs into sensitive systems. By addressing this underexplored security challenge, our research aims to encourage further research into the responsible use of LVLMs.

title: Class-matched antibiotic dispensing and susceptibility transitions in recurrent urinary gram-negative bacilli
abstractText: Objectives Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among urinary Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) is rising in Saudi Arabia, but how interim antibiotic exposure relates to within-patient changes in susceptibility is not well characterized. We evaluated the association between class-matched antibiotic exposure occurring between consecutive cultures and susceptible (S)-to-non-susceptible (NS) and non-susceptible-to-susceptible transitions. Methods In a single-center, retrospective, culture-based, pharmacy-linked paired-culture cohort at a 500-bed tertiary hospital in southern Saudi Arabia (Aseer Central Hospital [ACH]), consecutive same-patient, same-species urinary GNB cultures 14–365 days apart formed pairs, and interim exposure was defined as ACH-recorded antibiotic dispensing. For each of the seven feasible phenotypes, adjusted transition models estimated S→NS odds and separate direct models estimated NS→S odds, with supporting analyses using inverse probability weighting, cross-class models, E-values, penalized-likelihood sensitivity analyses, and exploratory pragmatic null-covariable diagnostics. Results The primary cohort comprised 1,274 pairs from 1,078 patients, of whom 807 (74.9%) had at least one interim ACH-recorded systemic antibiotic dispensing. Class-matched dispensing was associated with higher adjusted odds of an S→NS transition for extended-spectrum cephalosporins (OR, 3.83), difficult-to-treat resistance (OR, 2.91), piperacillin–tazobactam (OR, 2.46), and fluoroquinolones (OR, 2.29), but not carbapenems (OR, 0.93). In direct models, matched dispensing was associated with lower odds of an NS→S transition, reaching significance only for piperacillin–tazobactam (OR, 0.39). Conclusions In recurrent urinary GNB, interim class-matched hospital-recorded antibiotic dispensing was associated with within-patient S→NS transitions for several clinically important phenotypes. These observational associations do not establish treatment effects; they identify patterns for confirmation in prospective studies and may inform surveillance and stewardship evaluation.

title: Navigating the Shift to Self-Access Learning: Students’ Experiences in a Flipped EFL Writing Course
abstractText: Developing learner autonomy remains a central goal of self-access language learning, yet many English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners experience difficulties regulating independent learning. This study investigated students’ experiences with a semi-structured pre-class self-access learning approach implemented in a flipped EFL writing course. During a six-week intervention, 58 undergraduate students in a Thai university independently selected learning resources and strategies, and synthesized information through reflective notebook writing. A mixed-methods descriptive design was employed, combining questionnaire data with focus group discussions to examine students’ perceptions, challenges, and learning strategies. Overall, students reported positive perceptions of learning preparation, information management, learning responsibility, and writing readiness. However, they also experienced challenges related to limited linguistic knowledge, evaluating multiple resources, and regulating independent learning. Students addressed these challenges through planning, reflective notetaking, strategic help-seeking, and critical use of multiple learning resources, including GenAI. The findings suggest that semi-structured self-access learning, supported by pedagogical scaffolding, can provide a structured context for exercising learner autonomy while promoting self-regulated learning and emerging GenAI literacy.

title: Anatomical location matters: risk modelling and surgical outcomes in central lymph node metastasis of isthmus PTC
abstractText: Background Isthmus papillary thyroid carcinoma (iPTC) represents a distinct clinical entity with a higher propensity for central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) and greater local aggressiveness compared to lobe-confined PTC. Despite increasing recognition of its unique risk profile, controversy persists regarding optimal surgical management, particularly for small or indolent tumours. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 319 patients with histologically confirmed iPTC who underwent comprehensive ultrasonographic assessment and thyroid surgery from February 2019 to June 2024 at a high-volume tertiary centre. Lobe-confined PTC cases were matched as controls using propensity score methodology. Clinicopathological features, risk factors for CLNM, surgical outcomes, and recurrence patterns were analysed using univariate and multivariate analyses and ROC/AUC modelling. A predictive nomogram for CLNM was developed and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples with optimism correction. Results The iPTC cohort exhibited a significantly higher CLNM burden than matched lobe-confined PTC controls, independent of tumour size or multiplicity. Multivariate analysis identified male sex, increased isthmus tumour diameter, and calcification as independent preoperative predictors of CLNM. The derived nomogram demonstrated acceptable discrimination (optimism-corrected AUC 0.722, 95% CI 0.645–0.802) and internal calibration. Surgical extent (total thyroidectomy versus less extensive resection) was associated with increased perioperative morbidity but did not improve early recurrence rates in selected cases. There were no lymph node or distant recurrences on intermediate-term follow-up. Conclusions Isthmus location independently increases central nodal metastatic risk in PTC. Risk modelling with simple clinical and ultrasonographic factors quantifies the probability of central lymph node metastasis and highlights the trade-off between more extensive thyroid resection and increased perioperative morbidity. We did not observe an early recurrence or survival advantage associated with more extensive surgery in this cohort, within the limits of intermediate follow-up and routine central dissection; instead, they support individualised, risk-adapted decision-making that requires validation in prospective outcome studies.

Reentrant Phenomenon and Tunable Magnetic Transitions in Monolayer Graphyne-like Nanostructures: A Monte Carlo Study
abstractText: The magnetic properties of the monolayer graphyne-like nanostructures (MGLN) with mixed spins (S=1 and σ=7/2) are investigated by Monte Carlo simulation within the Blume-Capel model. The performed Monte Carlo simulations have produced some interesting features displaying the reentrant phenomenon. A detailed analysis of the system reveals the complex nature of its phase transitions with significant tunability in magnetism. Notably, a first-order to second-order magnetic transition crossover governed by T or H has been found in the system. These findings will be useful for understanding controllable magnetic responses in MGLN and for further spintronic and technological applications.

title: Caregiver burden and malnutrition in patients with HIV-associated lymphoma: indirect pathways via symptom distress and family closeness, and a test of resilience as a mediator
abstractText: Background and objective Malnutrition is a frequent and clinically significant complication in patients with HIV-associated lymphoma, adversely affecting treatment tolerance, prognosis, and quality of life. Although disease-related and immunological determinants of malnutrition have been widely reported, the potential psychosocial pathways—particularly the role of caregiver burden—in patients with HIV-associated lymphoma remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to identify key determinants of malnutrition and to examine whether caregiver burden exerts indirect effects through symptom distress and psychosocial factors. Methods This single-center cross-sectional study included 200 patients with HIV-associated lymphoma and their family caregivers. Nutritional status was assessed using the Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA), with the total score analyzed as a continuous outcome. Symptom burden, caregiver burden, psychological resilience, and family closeness were assessed using standardized instruments. Univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses were conducted using HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent inference. Indirect statistical associations were examined using bootstrap analyses, followed by exploratory subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Results Higher symptom burden and IPI risk were associated with higher PG-SGA total scores, whereas higher CD4 + T-cell counts and serum albumin concentrations were associated with lower scores (all p ≤ 0.005). Age, sex, and caregiver burden were not independently associated with PG-SGA score. Exploratory analyses provided no statistically supported evidence of an indirect association through symptom burden or of differences by age, sex, or CD4 + T-cell count. Sensitivity analyses produced consistent conclusions. Conclusion Nutritional status in patients with HIV-associated lymphoma was associated mainly with symptom burden, immune status, serum albumin, and lymphoma prognostic risk. Caregiver burden showed neither an independent association with PG-SGA score nor a confirmed indirect association through symptom burden. Larger multicenter longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationships among caregiver burden, psychosocial factors, and nutritional status.
